replay_bundle.scope: The immutable statement, accepted T23 and collision bridges, all five T24 primary sources and text extractions, the complete accepted T5 package, and every content-addressed object named by T5 or T24 are retained in this archive. No surrounding workspace or knowledge_library directory is required for replay.

canonical_target.statement: For every integer k >= 1 and every decimal word w of length k, including leading-zero words, liminf as N tends to infinity of A_pi(w,N)/N is strictly positive.

T23.definition_locator: E_pi lines 32-36; PiFullDimensionalCylinderEnergyDecay lines 38-45; quantifier audit lines 47-55; E_pi_eq_normalizedPiCylinderCollisionEnergy lines 467-475
T23.exact_quantifiers: For every real s with 0 < s < 1, there exist a real C >= 1 and a natural N0 such that for every natural N >= N0 and every natural m >= 1, E_pi(m,N) <= C*(10^(-s*m) + 1/N). C and N0 may depend on s, but not on N or m.
T23.scope_warning: T23 proves only this hypothesis implies C1; it does not prove the hypothesis for pi.

finite_energy_source.locators: piCylinderCollisionEnergy lines 36-47; diagonal lower bound lines 173-197; comparison theorem lines 292-345
finite_energy_source.statement: T7 proves normalizedPiCylinderCollisionEnergy(m,N) <= Q_pi(m,N)/N^2 <= 3*normalizedPiCylinderCollisionEnergy(m,N). T23 lines 467-475 identify its E_pi with that normalized energy.

variables.m: positive decimal cylinder length and near-return exponent

generic_translation.structured_denominator: Q(n,r)=10^n*(10^r-1), for n >= 0 and r >= 1; hence Q >= 9.
generic_translation.source_form: If |pi-p/q| >= q^(-mu) for the applicable p,q, then ||Q*pi|| >= Q^(1-mu). Strict source inequalities remain strict.
generic_translation.pair_exclusion: The strict near return at radius 10^(-m) is excluded whenever the source denominator condition holds and m >= a*(n+log10(10^r-1)).
generic_translation.simple_sufficient_region: Since log10(10^r-1)<r, m >= a*(n+r) is a simpler sufficient exclusion condition.
generic_translation.global_energy_translation: For a bound valid at every Q>=9, put L=min(N-1,floor(m/a)). Every unordered pair with upper index n+r<=L is excluded, so Q_pi(m,N)<=N^2-L*(L+1) and E_pi(m,N)<=1-L*(L+1)/N^2. If m>=a*(N-1), only the N diagonal pairs remain and E_pi(m,N)=1/N.
generic_translation.scale_mismatch: For m=o(N), the retained upper bound tends to 1 rather than to 0. In particular m=floor(sqrt(N)) leaves order N^2 unresolved pairs, while T23 requires an upper bound tending to 0 for every fixed 0<s<1.

verdict_policy.FULL: The cited theorem, with every premise discharged, proves T23's exact every-s, all-later-N, all-positive-m energy hypothesis.
verdict_policy.PARTIAL: The cited theorem unconditionally applies to fixed pi on a nonempty, explicitly displayed denominator or scale region, but leaves part of T23's (n,r,m,N) range unresolved.
verdict_policy.NONE: The cited theorem has no unconditional fixed-pi consequence for the requested structured denominators or has an indispensable scope mismatch.
verdict_policy.C1_rule: PARTIAL scale control neither proves nor supports C1. C1 may be claimed only after the complete T23 hypothesis or another verified sufficient premise is discharged.

rows.exact_source_statement: For all positive integers p and q with p>=2 and q>=2, |pi-p/q|>q^(-42).
rows.denominator_scope: All q>=2; no eventual onset. For Q(n,r)>=9 the nearest numerator is positive and at least 2.
rows.controlled_region: Every pair with m>=41*(n+log10(10^r-1)); in particular every pair with n+r<=m/41.
rows.unresolved_region: Pairs with m<41*(n+log10(10^r-1)); for an N-prefix this includes almost all pairs whenever m=o(N).
rows.prefix_consequence: With L=min(N-1,floor(m/41)), E_pi(m,N)<=1-L*(L+1)/N^2; if m>=41*(N-1), E_pi(m,N)=1/N.
rows.T23_comparison: The theorem controls a fine region linear in N, not every m>=1. It supplies no T23 constants C(s),N0(s) valid for all later N and all m.
rows.C1_consequence: None. Partial scale control neither proves nor supports C1.

rows.locator: Theoreme 1, printed p. 125 (PDF page 6), first inequality
rows.exact_source_statement: For a positive rational p/q with q>=2, |pi-p/q|>q^(-20.6).
rows.denominator_scope: All q>=2. If p/Q is not reduced, applying the theorem to its reduced denominator q'<=Q only strengthens q'^(-20.6)>=Q^(-20.6).
rows.controlled_region: Every pair with m>=19.6*(n+log10(10^r-1)); in particular every pair with n+r<=m/19.6.
rows.unresolved_region: Pairs above the triangular boundary n+r>m/19.6. For m=o(N), order N^2 pairs remain uncontrolled.
rows.T23_comparison: This is the strongest retained all-denominator row, but T23 is all-m. The derived upper bound tends to 1 for m=o(N), whereas T23 requires full-dimensional decay.
rows.C1_consequence: None. Partial scale control neither proves nor supports C1.

rows.locator: Theoreme 1, printed p. 125 (PDF page 6), second inequality
rows.exact_source_statement: For a positive rational p/q with q>=exp(e^110), |pi-p/q|>q^(-20).
rows.denominator_scope: Explicit enormous onset Qstar=exp(e^110). The same theorem's first clause covers 2<=q<Qstar with exponent 20.6.
rows.controlled_region: Q>=Qstar and m>=19*(n+log10(10^r-1)); using the companion 20.6 clause, all prefix pairs are excluded if m>=max(19*(N-1),19.6*log10(Qstar)).
rows.unresolved_region: Below that fine-scale prefix boundary. The improved exponent does not control the all-m region m=o(N).
rows.prefix_consequence: Combining both clauses of Theoreme 1 gives E_pi(m,N)=1/N when m>=max(19*(N-1),19.6*e^110/log(10)).
rows.T23_comparison: The explicit onset removes ineffectivity but leaves a quantified scale mismatch: eventual collision freedom only when m is about 19N, not for all positive m.
rows.C1_consequence: None. Partial scale control neither proves nor supports C1.

rows.locator: Theorem 1.1 and its displayed pi corollary, printed p. 336
rows.exact_source_statement: Theorem 1.1 has: for every epsilon>0 there is H0(epsilon) such that |p+q*pi+r*log(2)|>=H^(-mu-epsilon), H=max(|q|,|r|)>=H0, with mu=7.016045... . The printed corollary states |pi-p/q|>=q^(-8.0161) for all integers p,q with q>=q0.
rows.denominator_scope: All q>=an existential q0; no numerical q0 is printed.
rows.unresolved_region: All Q<q0 lack a source-numerical patch, and all pairs below the displayed m boundary remain uncontrolled.
rows.prefix_consequence: No replayable numerical full-prefix frontier follows because q0 is unspecified; even after an existential finite patch the frontier is linear m approximately 7.0161N.
rows.T23_comparison: The fixed-pi result is genuine but has both an unspecified onset and the same all-m scale mismatch.
rows.C1_consequence: None. Partial scale control neither proves nor supports C1.

rows.locator: Theorem 1, p. 570, and final calculation, p. 571
rows.exact_source_statement: For all natural p,q with q>=q0, |pi-p/q|>=q^(-nu); the final calculation establishes the inequality for every fixed nu>7.60630852... . This row fixes nu=7.60630853.
rows.denominator_scope: All q>=an existential q0(7.60630853); no numerical q0 is printed.
rows.unresolved_region: Q<q0 and every pair below the displayed m boundary; most prefix pairs remain unresolved for m=o(N).
rows.prefix_consequence: After a non-numerical finite patch one would get collision freedom only above m=6.60630853*(N-1)+O(1), not at all scales.
rows.T23_comparison: The better exponent moves the linear boundary but supplies no aggregate bound in T23's complementary lag-scale region.
rows.C1_consequence: None. Partial scale control neither proves nor supports C1.

rows.locator: Irrationality-measure definition and title claim, p. 407; Propositions 7-8 and World record, pp. 417-418
rows.exact_source_statement: The irrationality measure of pi is at most 7.1032053341370017275... . By the source definition, fixing 7.104 gives an existential Q0 such that |pi-p/q|>q^(-7.104) for every integer p and all q>=Q0.
rows.denominator_scope: All q>=an existential Q0(7.104); the paper does not print a numerical onset. No endpoint claim at 7.103205... is used.
rows.unresolved_region: Q<Q0(7.104) is not numerically delimited, and all pairs below the displayed m boundary remain uncontrolled.
rows.prefix_consequence: Even granting an existential finite patch, collision freedom occurs only above m=6.104*(N-1)+O(1). For m=o(N), the theorem leaves order N^2 pairs unresolved.
rows.T23_comparison: This is the best retained exponent but not a full T23 input: it has an unspecified onset and controls individual separation only in a fine linear-scale region.
rows.C1_consequence: None. Partial scale control neither proves nor supports C1.

bounded_conclusion: There is no FULL row. Every retained theorem gives a genuine fixed-pi exclusion region, so each is PARTIAL rather than NONE, but none bounds the aggregate unresolved pairs at all positive m. The explicit Mignotte theorem yields E_pi(m,N)=1/N only at m at least about 19N; the best eventual exponent lowers this to about 6.104N after an unspecified onset. T23 requires every m>=1 for all later N and every 0<s<1. Therefore this corpus does not prove or support C1.
